name: Khumbu Himalaya (Everest region)
region: Nepal/Tibet Himalaya from Manaslu to Kangchenjunga; also used for Bhutan.
sources: Matthews, T. et al. (2020) Going to Extremes: Installing the World's Highest Weather Stations on Mount Everest. BAMS 101(11)
Perry, L. B. et al. (2020) Precipitation characteristics and moisture source regions on Mt. Everest in the Khumbu, Nepal. One Earth 3(5)
Salerno, F. et al. (2015) Weak precipitation, warm winters and springs impact glaciers of south slopes of Mt. Everest. The Cryosphere 9 (Pyramid station 5050 m)
Hersbach, H. et al. (2020) The ERA5 global reanalysis. QJRMS 146:1999-2049 (monthly climatology 1991-2020, 300 hPa winds)
notes: Monsoon (Jun-Sep) brings most precipitation; winter jet stream over the summit exceeds 45 m/s. Pre-monsoon summit windows open in mid/late May when the subtropical jet migrates north.
